2	  "title": "feat(workspaces): part 4 — per-workspace cloud, Assign to workspace, synced-folder safety (NIW2-602)",
3	  "body": "## Summary

Part 4 of several workspaces: Kaipu Cloud per workspace, "Assign to workspace…", and safety for workspace folders inside Google Drive, OneDrive or iCloud Drive.

- Linear: [NIW2-602](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-602) (part 4) and [NIW2-577](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-577) (drag-out hard links rename or unsync items in a Google Drive library).
- **Stacked on #482** (part 3, NIW2-601), which is stacked on #479 → #478. Base: `feature/niw2-601-workspaces-part-3-settings`. The latest part-3 head (`543053c4`) is merged in.
- Spec: `specs/2026-10-29-several-workspaces-design.md`. The orphan rule as built, the deploy order and what part 4 leaves out are now written in its "Cloud: server and client" and "Synced folders" sections.

## Server

- `cloud_asset.workspace_id`: nullable `text`, no foreign key, no rewrite of existing rows. Migration `0003_cloud_asset_workspace_id.sql` is one `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN`.
- `POST /assets/upload-intents` takes an optional `workspaceId`. A re-upload without one keeps the asset's current workspace, and an older desktop that sends none is still accepted.
- `GET /assets` and every asset summary include `workspaceId`.
- `PUT /assets/{assetId}/workspace` with `{ workspaceId: string | null }`: owner-only (another account's asset answers 404), validated (a plain id, max 64 chars, or `null` to unassign), idempotent.

**About the migration file.** On `main`, schema changes still ship with `db:push` (`commands.md`). Committed migrations exist only in the open #364 (ADR 0029, Proposed), so I generated this migration with `drizzle-kit generate` on top of #364's chain, offline, as `0003`. The journal here lists `0000`–`0003`; whichever of #364 and this PR merges second resolves `meta/_journal.json` to the four-entry version. Until #364 lands, the column goes out with `db:push`. No migration was run against any database.

## Desktop

**Cloud filter.** This replaces the part-1 stopgap (`ownsLegacyCloud`). The Library composes with a view of the catalog filtered to the active workspace; the cache file keeps every workspace's entries, and `lastSeenLocalId` updates merge into it inside the cache's write chain (`CatalogCache.update`). The rule, in `main/cloud/workspace-filter.ts`:

1. An entry's workspace is the server's `workspaceId`; an assignment still owed to the server wins over it.
2. The active workspace lists its own entries, plus the cloud copy of any of its local items.
3. Unassigned entries (`workspace_id = null`) show in the migrated Default workspace **until the user's first "Assign to workspace…"**, so nothing disappears on upgrade. After that first assignment they show only under Cloud → "Unassigned cloud items".
4. Entries of a workspace not registered on this Mac show in no Library, only in that list. Nothing is assigned automatically.

**Moves.** After a move commits, its cloud asset gets `PUT …/workspace` through a persisted retry queue (`userData/cloud-assign-queue.json`, backoff from 30 s to 1 h, also flushed after a catalog refresh). It never blocks or fails the move. Until the server confirms, the owed assignment overlays the catalog, so an offline move never shows the item in its old workspace.

**Uploads.** The desktop upload flow (NIW2-214) has not shipped, so no upload calls the server today. `main/cloud/upload-intent-client.ts` is the request that flow will use; its type makes `workspaceId` required.

**Cloud page → "This workspace".** Shows where the folder lives (This Mac, an external drive, or the detected provider), which Kaipu Cloud items its Library lists, and the unassigned cloud items with "Assign to workspace…" and "Assign all to workspace…".

**Synced folders** (decision 15, NIW2-577):
- **Detection:** by path after `realpath` (`~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…`, `OneDrive…`, `~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs`), plus Google Drive's xattr `com.google.drivefs.item-id#S` on `identity.json`. Each step is bounded at 2 s. The provider is named on the Cloud page, in the switcher and on the Settings → Workspaces row.
- **Scratch files:** recording staging, move staging and drag copies go to `userData/workspace-scratch/<id>/`, never `.kaipu/tmp/` or `.kaipu/drag/`. The startup and quit sweeps cover them.
- **No hard links:** drag copies are real copies, and takes are placed by `rename`, not `link()`. A move with a synced side copies, verifies sha256 **at the final path**, then deletes, even when `stat.dev` matches (the "Move to" menu says "Synced folder · copies").
- **Evicted files:** detected by `SF_DATALESS` from one `/usr/bin/stat -f '%f %N'` call per listing. Zero blocks is only a fallback when that call returns nothing. An evicted file gets no thumbnail URL, `kaipu-media://` answers 409 without opening a stream, the orphan heal skips it, and it cannot be dragged or moved ("In the cloud: download it first").
- **Availability probe:** bounded at 5 s and never lists the provider root. A probe that does not answer while `stat` still sees the folder leaves the workspace available but "unverified": nothing can be moved into it until a later probe answers.

**Did the move's same-volume path hit the hard-link problem?** Yes. Part 2 linked the media and the companion files whenever `stat.dev` matched, and on the internal drive it always matches. A synced side now always takes the copy+verify path, staged in userData, placed by rename into a synced target. Tests cover a synced source, target and both, a mismatch at the final path, and a crash healed from the scratch folder.

## Deploy order

**The desktop tolerates the server's absence**, so the two can ship in either order (tested):
- A server without the route answers Hono's plain-text 404 or a 405. The desktop reads that as `unsupported` (`assign-client.test.ts`) and keeps the assignment queued; the Library still shows the item in its new workspace (`assign-queue.test.ts`, "a server without the endpoint is tolerated").
- A real missing asset answers JSON `code: NOT_FOUND` (asserted in `asset-workspace.contract.test.ts`) and is dropped.
- A `GET /assets` without `workspaceId` reads as null (`catalog-client.test.ts`).
- The server accepts an upload intent without `workspaceId`.

Recommended order anyway: server migration, then the server deploy, then the desktop release.

## Deviations from the mock (Kaipu Workspaces v2, section 4 "CLOUD")

The spec wins over the mock: Google Drive and OneDrive are not providers Kaipu syncs to.

1. **No provider picker.** The mock's radio list (Kaipu Cloud / Google Drive / OneDrive / Local only, "Each workspace picks its own") is replaced by a read-only "Where it lives" row with the detected location.
2. **No provider status line.** "Connected · acme.com · /Kaipu Captures" and "Up to date · 42 items · last sync 2 min ago" are gone: Kaipu does not talk to the provider.
3. **Kaipu Cloud stays per account,** not a per-workspace choice. The page shows instead which Kaipu Cloud items this workspace's Library lists.
4. **No "Personal stays on this Mac. Share links are off here." banner.** Local-only per workspace is the save-mode override from part 3, and share links do not exist yet.
5. **Not in the mock:** the filter row and the "Unassigned cloud items" list with "Assign to workspace…" / "Assign all to workspace…" (from the spec).
6. **Placement:** the section sits below the account and save-mode blocks, under the workspace's own name and tile, instead of a "Cloud · PER WORKSPACE" page title.
7. **Switcher:** the mock gives each workspace a "cloud" label ("Google Drive", "Kaipu Cloud", "Local only"). Here a synced folder's provider replaces "This Mac" in the location part of the row ("17 items · Google Drive"), and nothing says "Kaipu Cloud", since that is the account's.

## Not in this PR

- The **Download** action (`workspaces:download-item`). An evicted item shows "In the cloud" with a hint to download it in Finder.
- The conflict-copy warning, and the one-time note when a synced folder is added (the Cloud page shows the note for as long as the workspace is synced).
- Moving a **cloud-only** item, and the `orphanCloudCount` field of `workspaces:list`.
- `placeByRename` checks the destination with `lstat`, then renames. Node has no rename-without-replace, so a file created at that exact, just-reserved name in between would be replaced. This is written in `safe-place.ts` and in the spec.
- The `kaipu-media://` eviction gate runs only while the active workspace is synced.

## Verification

- Typechecks: desktop node + web, `server-hono`, `domain`, `application`, `infra-db`, all clean. `oxlint`: 0 errors, no warnings in changed files. `oxfmt --check .`: clean.
- Unit tests: desktop 406 files / 4,626 tests; `server-hono` 97; `application` 62; `domain` 68.
- `stat`, the xattr and the File Provider are mocked in every test. The real Google Drive was not touched.
- **Not run:** Electron, Playwright and `/verify` (owner rule: no local E2E on this machine). The `infra-db` integration suite needs `TEST_DATABASE_URL`: a case for `setWorkspace` and the reserve's `coalesce` is added but was not run. No migration was run against any database.

## How to test it yourself

**Server** (a throwaway database or a Neon branch only):
1. Apply the column (`bun run db:push` against the dev database, or run `0003_cloud_asset_workspace_id.sql`).
2. With a signed-in token, `curl -X PUT …/api/v1/assets/<assetId>/workspace -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"workspaceId":"<a workspace id>"}'` should return the summary with `workspaceId`.
3. The same call with `null` clears it. Another account's asset answers 404. `{"workspaceId":"../x"}` answers 400.
4. `GET /api/v1/assets` shows `workspaceId` on each item.

**Desktop, plain folders:**
1. Open Cloud. "This workspace" shows the active workspace, "Where it lives: This Mac", and "This workspace's, plus the unassigned ones" on the Default workspace.
2. Signed in with cloud items uploaded before this version: they show in the Default workspace's Library and under "Unassigned cloud items". Switch to another workspace: they are not in its Library.
3. Assign one to Work. It leaves the list and Default's Library and shows in Work's. From then on, the remaining unassigned items show only in the list (the filter row now says "Only this workspace's").
4. Move an item that has a cloud copy to another workspace while offline. Its cloud copy follows it at once. Back online, after a Library refresh, the server holds the new `workspaceId`.

**Desktop, a Google Drive folder** (a scratch workspace in `My Drive`):
1. Add it. Cloud says "Synced by Google Drive", and so does its Settings → Workspaces row.
2. Record a take: `ls "<folder>/.kaipu/tmp"` shows nothing while it records; the `.part` is under `~/Library/Application Support/<app>/workspace-scratch/<id>/tmp/`.
3. Drag an item out by its title, then `stat -f %l "<folder>/<item>.mp4"` prints `1`, and the item keeps its name in Drive.
4. In Finder, "Remove Download" on a screenshot. Reopen the Library: the card says "In the cloud", its "⋯" menu says "In the cloud: download it first", and `stat -f %f` on the file still shows the `0x40000000` bit.
5. "Move to" another workspace says "Synced folder · copies", and the moved file is byte-identical (`shasum -a 256` on both sides).

content.text: Checking the order of sync detection and the Library re-list for an active relocate: confirming where the Library listing reads the eviction probe.

findings.title: Relocating the active workspace re-lists the Library before the new folder's sync provider is detected
findings.body:
For the active workspace, `relocateWorkspace` goes through `relocateActive` (`relocate.ts:46-48`). On commit, that calls `afterCommit` (`switch-transaction.ts:136`), which runs `host?.broadcastLibraryChanged()` (`index.ts:524-530`). So the windows re-list the Library **before** `syncStates.refresh(current)` runs here at line 755.

Until the refresh settles, `syncStates.of(active)` sees a path that differs from the cached one and falls back to `syncProviderOfPath(entry.path)` (`sync-state.ts:26-30`). That check does no `realpath` and no xattr read. A folder that only `detectSync` recognises gets `null` from it: a Drive folder reached through a symlink, or Drive mounted somewhere else and caught only by `com.google.drivefs.item-id#S` (`synced-folder.ts:80-91`). In that case `activeEvictionProbe()` returns null, and `LibraryVault` is built without a probe (`library/index.ts:72-74`). Evicted files are then listed as local and get thumbnail URLs, and the "In the cloud: download it first" state never shows.

After the refresh, this handler only calls `broadcastState()` (line 759). Nothing triggers another Library re-list, so the wrong listing stays until something else refreshes it. Nothing tells the user.

The sibling handlers detect first: `addWorkspace` refreshes at line 578 before `runSwitch` at 601, and `createWorkspace` refreshes at 630 before 635. Two possible fixes:
- Detect the provider of `chosen` before the transaction commits.
- Call `host?.broadcastLibraryChanged()` after the refresh when the relocated workspace is the active one.

I marked this medium confidence because it depends on the renderer's list request arriving before `realpath` plus the `/usr/bin/xattr` exec finish, and I did not measure that.

input.summary: The new `relocateFolder` lines detect the relocated folder's sync provider before the bounded availability probe and return a `workspace` view, as `WorkspaceRelocateResult` requires. One ordering problem: when the active workspace is relocated, `afterCommit` re-lists the Library before `syncStates.refresh` runs, and nothing re-lists it afterwards. A synced folder that only `realpath` or the Drive xattr can identify can therefore be listed without the eviction probe. The two earlier threads (migration journal and snapshot) are on files outside this part, so they get no replies here.
